title: Procedural Graphs let agents revise the order and conditions of their own workflows
friendlyTitle: Researchers gave agents a workflow map that can improve after failures
summary: A new preprint proposes Procedural Graphs, which represent agent know-how as linked procedures describing what to do, in what order and under which conditions. A refiner compares successful and failed trajectories, edits the graph and retains changes only when they preserve or improve held-out validation performance.
friendlySummary: The system stores steps and conditions in a graph instead of leaving the whole plan inside a long chat history. It compares good and bad runs, then keeps only workflow changes that pass tests.
whyItMatters: Explicit procedures can make long-running agents easier to inspect and less dependent on an ever-growing conversation history. The method is still a preprint, but the design principle is practical now: externalize workflow state, learn from failures and validate changes before promoting them.
friendlyWhyItMatters: A visible workflow is easier to inspect and repair than hidden reasoning. Record steps clearly and test every change before using it in real work.
